changelog: Fixed a second, independent source of migrate.php's SQLSTATE[HY000] 2014 ('unbuffered queries are active') crash on mode=run — v3.21.10 closed the schema_migrations tracking-table cursor, but mode=run against the pending backtest migrations still hit the identical error, now inside recordMigration()'s own execute(). Root cause: the per-statement loop ran every migration statement through $db->exec(), which returns only an int/false — no handle to closeCursor() on. Every guarded-ALTER migration's own no-op fallback ('EXECUTE stmt' where the dynamically prepared SQL is the literal 'SELECT 1', taken whenever the guard finds the column already exists — exactly the case on a retry of a migration that partially applied before an earlier crash) genuinely returns a resultset from the server, and exec() has no way to drain or close it. That left an unread result sitting on the connection until the next statement requiring the connection idle, which was recordMigration() again.

Fixed by switching the per-statement loop from $db->exec($statement) to $s = $db->query($statement); $s->closeCursor();. query() always returns a real PDOStatement, closed immediately regardless of whether that particular statement happens to return rows — this guards every current statement shape in the guarded-ALTER pattern (SET/PREPARE/EXECUTE/DEALLOCATE/ALTER/CREATE/UPDATE) uniformly, and any future one, without needing to special-case which statements might return a resultset.

PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY => true is being set directly in includes/config.php on the server as the primary, connection-level fix for this whole class of bug — outside this repo, config.php is never committed (§13 rule 4). This release's migrate.php change is defense in depth: it closes the two specific leaks found so far even if buffered mode is ever off for any reason, but is not a substitute for that connection-level setting.

No database was touched and mode=run was not executed as part of this release, per instruction. See CLAUDE.md's new v3.21.11 section for the full trace of every DB call in the mode=run path and why only this one statement shape was at risk.
release_notes: Code-only fix to migrate.php, shipped alongside a config.php change Acrob is applying directly on the server (PDO::MYSQL_ATTR_USE_BUFFERED_QUERY => true, not in this repo). After Update Now, migrate.php?mode=status then mode=run can be attempted again for the 4 pending backtest migrations (2026_09_25_0002 through 2026_09_26_0003).
